field.label: Enabled
field.help: Enable this instance. Disabled instances are skipped on start and reconfigure.

field.label: Name
field.help: Display name for this instance in the table

field.label: Config Source
field.help: Where the xray-core config comes from. "Xray config (JSON)" — the outbound JSON below, the backend wraps it with TUN/SOCKS/routing sections. "Server group" — one server of a group (or, with Load Balancing, all servers of the group). "Server only" — no upstream: the instance just accepts incoming connections (see Server Inbound). "Custom full config" — the entire config.json below is used verbatim.

field.label: Outbound Config (JSON)
field.help: xray-core outbound object (Config Source = Xray config). Use "Import VLESS link" above to auto-fill, or paste/write the outbound JSON directly.

field.label: Server Group
field.help: Group to pick the node from. With Load Balancing enabled, ALL servers of this group become balancer members. Managed on the Groups tab.

field.label: Server
field.help: Active node of the selected group (used when Load Balancing is off). Changing it rewrites config.json and restarts this instance only.

field.label: Full Config (Raw JSON)
field.help: Full xray-core config.json used verbatim (Config Source = Custom full config). Validate the draft with the "Validate Config" button before saving. Note: with the tun2socks legacy TUN driver the config must contain a SOCKS inbound at the configured port.

field.label: TUN Driver
field.help: "Xray TUN inbound (native)" — the TUN interface is created by xray-core itself (protocol "tun", requires xray-core 26.10+; on FreeBSD the interface name must be tunN). "tun2socks (legacy)" — the external tun2socks daemon forwarding the TUN to the SOCKS inbound.

field.label: TUN Interface
field.help: TUN interface name. Native driver on FreeBSD: must match tunN, e.g. tun100. Must match the name in Interfaces → Assignments.

field.label: TUN Gateway (CIDR)
field.help: On FreeBSD xray assigns the interface the address right after the gateway (e.g. 10.255.0.1/30 → interface gets 10.255.0.2/30); the gateway itself is routed into the TUN. Use it as the OPNsense "Far Gateway" and set the interface static IP to gateway+1 with the same mask.

field.label: MTU
field.help: Maximum Transmission Unit for the TUN interface
field.hint: Default: 1500. Reduce to 1380 if large packets (e.g. SSH, large downloads) fail or are slow.

field.label: System Routing
field.help: "Off" — choose what goes through the tunnel with OPNsense firewall rules and the TUN gateway (selective). "Full tunnel" — xray itself installs the system default route (minus protected ranges) and keeps its own connections out of the TUN via a second routing table; requires net.fibs=2 in /boot/loader.conf and a reboot. No OPNsense gateway needed in this mode.

field.label: System DNS → TUN (full mode)
field.help: Only for Full tunnel: hand the router's own resolver (resolvconf) to the TUN gateway so local lookups go through Xray. Do not combine with unbound DNSSEC validation. Requires the DNS hijack rule (generated automatically).

field.label: Enable SOCKS5
field.help: Local SOCKS5 inbound. Used by the legacy tun2socks driver, by "Test connection" and by local applications (e.g. curl --socks5). Can be disabled for pure TUN or pure server-mode instances.

field.label: SOCKS5 Listen Address
field.help: IP address xray-core binds for its SOCKS5 inbound.

field.label: SOCKS5 Port
field.help: Local port xray-core binds for its SOCKS5 inbound
field.hint: Default: 10808. Must not be used by another process or the server inbound.

field.label: DNS Mode
field.help: "Hijack" — DNS queries (port 53) entering the tunnel are answered by Xray itself using the upstream below and leave through the proxy (no DNS leak for full tunnel). "Off" — no dns block; OPNsense/unbound keeps handling DNS.

field.label: DNS Upstream
field.help: Nameserver used by the built-in DNS (hijack mode).

field.label: Enable Balancer
field.help: Route proxied traffic through a balancer with background health checks (burstObservatory). Members: all servers of the selected group (Config Source = Server group) or the custom list below. Unmatched traffic uses the balancer too.

field.label: Strategy
field.help: leastPing — pick the lowest latency alive node. roundRobin — rotate over alive nodes. leastLoad — combine latency, jitter and loss (advanced settings via raw JSON). random — random alive node.

field.label: Probe URL
field.help: URL used for the background health checks of the balancer.

field.label: Probe Interval
field.help: Health check interval (Go duration, e.g. 30s, 1m, 5m).

field.label: Custom Outbound List (JSON)
field.help: Used with Load Balancing when Config Source = Xray config: JSON array of outbound objects, each becomes a balancer member. Ignored in group mode.

field.label: Enable Incoming VLESS
field.help: Accept incoming proxy connections (the engine works as a VLESS server), e.g. fronted by nginx. Combine with routing rules on inboundTag "vless-in" for per-domain routing of incoming clients.

field.label: Listen Address
field.help: 127.0.0.1 when fronted by nginx on this box; 0.0.0.0 or a WAN/LAN IP for direct exposure.

field.label: Listen Port
field.help: Port for the incoming VLESS inbound (nginx forwards here). Must differ from the SOCKS5 port.

field.label: Users (JSON)
field.help: Clients allowed to connect: [{"id":"<uuid>","email":"user1","flow":""}]. Use the "Add user" button below the editor to append a generated UUID.

field.label: Transport
field.help: WebSocket is the usual choice behind an nginx reverse proxy; gRPC also works behind nginx (grpc_pass); TCP/HTTP2 for direct exposure.

field.label: Path / Service Name
field.help: WebSocket path or gRPC serviceName (h2 path). Must match the nginx location.

field.label: Security
field.help: "None" — TLS is terminated by nginx in front (recommended). "TLS" — xray terminates TLS itself with the certificate files below. "Reality" — direct exposure without nginx (TCP only).

field.label: TLS Certificate File
field.help: Absolute path to the certificate (PEM), e.g. from the ACME plugin. Used with Security = TLS.

field.label: TLS Key File
field.help: Absolute path to the private key (PEM). Used with Security = TLS.

field.label: Reality Private Key
field.help: x25519 private key (base64) for the Reality server. Generate with: xray-core x25519.

field.label: Reality Short IDs
field.help: Comma-separated hex short IDs allowed for clients, e.g. "" (empty allowed), abcdef01.

field.label: Reality Server Names
field.help: Comma-separated SNI values clients may use.

field.label: Reality Dest (fallback)
field.help: Fallback target for non-Reality handshakes, e.g. example.com:443. Required with Reality.

field.label: Accept PROXY Protocol
field.help: Enable when nginx forwards with proxy_protocol on (stream or http). Keeps the real client IP.

field.label: Additional Inbounds (JSON)
field.help: JSON array of arbitrary xray inbound objects merged into the config (vmess, trojan, shadowsocks, dokodemo-door, another vless, ...). Each object needs a unique "tag".

field.label: Incoming Traffic Default
field.help: Where traffic of incoming clients goes when no routing rule matches it (rules on inboundTag "vless-in" take precedence). "proxy" chains incoming users through the upstream; with Load Balancing it goes through the balancer.

field.label: Xray Log Level
field.help: Verbosity of xray-core internal logs
field.hint: warning is recommended for production. Use debug only for troubleshooting — it generates a lot of output.
